about: Cues made from generated sources instead of synthesis (Tools/AudioGen/Recorded.cs). Each entry replaces the synthesized cue of the same name; SFX_CoinCollect_01 has no synthesized version and is made from its source alone. Sound effects: ElevenLabs Sound Effects, 1 October 2026 (CoinCollect: 9 October 2026), 48 kHz WAV downloads, prompt influence 60%, durations as given. Music: Gemini 'Create music', 26 October 2026, two upbeat desi game-music tracks (Standard length, Instrumental), MP3 downloads decoded to 44.1 kHz WAV with Windows Media Foundation (Tools/AudioGen/decode-mp3.ps1); they replaced the Nepali folk loops of 1 October 2026, whose sources were deleted at the owner's word (ADR 049; in git history before that). To try another take, change 'source' and run: dotnet run --project Tools/AudioGen -c Release

SFX_CoinCollect_01.note: Every take ends in a few-ms burst, so max makes the cut. take1: eleven clinks in 0.55 s, quiet by 0.65 s. take2 rattles on to 1.0 s and needs max 1.05 (it then imports as a Vorbis sting).

MUS_Menu_Theme.note: Gemini's 'Table of Kings' (26 Oct 2026): about 104 BPM; 50 bars of 4 beats (115.35 s); found with Tools/AudioGen/find-loop.py (texture 0.86)

MUS_Table_Loop.note: Gemini's 'Copper Tiles' (26 Oct 2026): about 95 BPM; 40 bars of 4 beats (101.06 s); the track's steady part ends at 143 s, a quieter outro follows; found with Tools/AudioGen/find-loop.py (texture 0.72)

prompts.ElevenLabs/CardPlay: A single playing card tossed onto a felt-covered wooden card table: a quick crisp paper flick, then a soft flat pat as it lands and settles. Close-miked, dry studio foley, no reverb, no music, no voices. (0.5 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/CardDeal: One playing card dealt quickly off the top of a deck and slid across a felt card table: a short soft papery fft slide, ending in a light flick. Close-miked, dry studio foley, no reverb, no music, no voices. (0.5 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/CardShuffle: A deck of playing cards riffle-shuffled once on a table: a fast papery riffle, the two halves bridged together, and a soft tap as the deck is squared. Close-miked, dry studio foley, no reverb, no music, no voices. (1.2 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/TrickCollect: Four playing cards swept together across a felt card table into a neat pile: a soft sliding shhk of paper and a light pat as the small stack comes to rest. Close-miked, dry studio foley, no reverb, no music, no voices. (0.7 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/CallConfirm: A single soft muted wooden knock, like a fingertip tapping the wooden rim of a Nepali madal drum: warm, short, rounded and dry. One hit only. No reverb, no music, no voices. (0.5 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/YourTurn: A gentle friendly two-note rising chime on a soft wooden marimba, telling a player it is their turn in a calm card game: warm and round, a short soft ring, never urgent. Dry, no music, no voices. (1.0 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/TimerTick: One tiny dry wooden tick, like a small woodblock clock ticking once: very short, crisp and quiet. A single tick only. No reverb, no music, no voices. (automatic length)
prompts.ElevenLabs/CallMet: A short warm success chime: three soft bell tones rising into a gentle major chord, like small brass bells at a Nepali temple, pleasant and quiet with a short ring. No music, no voices. (1.2 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/CallMissed: A soft falling two-note muted tone, like a small tongue drum played under a cloth: a gentle sigh of disappointment when a player misses their call in a calm card game. Warm and low, short, not a buzzer and not comical. No music, no voices. (1.0 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/RoundEnd: A short descending chime phrase: four soft bell notes stepping down one after another and ringing out gently, marking the end of a round in a calm card game. Warm and quiet, like small temple bells. Nothing else, no music, no voices. (1.5 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/Victory: A short joyful Nepali celebration sting for winning a card game: a quick madal hand-drum roll building into two strong drum strokes, then a bright bansuri bamboo flute flourish that rises and resolves, festive like Dashain. About three seconds, no vocals. (3.0 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/UiTap: A small soft rounded wooden button tap for a mobile card game menu: one very short, clean and gentle tok, like a fingertip on a small wooden block. Dry, no echo, no ding, no plastic click, no music, no voices. (0.5 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/UiBack: A soft low wooden tap for going back or closing a screen in a mobile card game menu: one very short rounded tok, a little lower and softer than a button tap, slightly falling. Dry, no echo, no whoosh, no music, no voices. (0.5 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/Toggle: A tiny soft two-part wooden switch click, tk-tok, the second slightly lower, for flipping a settings toggle in a mobile card game menu. Very short and dry, no echo, no metal, no plastic snap, no music, no voices. (0.5 s)
prompts.ElevenLabs/CoinCollect: A short bright cascade of a few small gold coins dropping and clinking into a little pile, the cheerful reward sound of a mobile card game when coins land in the wallet: crisp, clean and close, light metallic clinks that settle quickly. Dry, no reverb, no music, no voices, no whoosh, no cash register bell. (1.3 s; 9 October 2026, loop off, 'automatically improves short or unclear prompts' on as the page had it; it kept the prompt as written)
prompts.Gemini/Table_of_Kings: Please make a new instrumental track: fun, polished mobile-game menu music with an Indian and Nepali flavour for a Callbreak card game lobby. A catchy sitar riff and a flute melody you can hum, tabla and dholak rhythms layered with modern hip-hop style drums, claps and round bass, bright synth plucks. Confident, happy and celebratory like a card game lobby, around 100 BPM, major key. Steady, loopable game music with the same energy throughout: no long intro, no breakdown, no ending, no vocals. (Create music: Standard, Instrumental, genre Custom; 26 October 2026)
prompts.Gemini/Copper_Tiles: Please make a new instrumental track: in-game background music for the card table of a mobile Callbreak game, in the same upbeat desi game-music style as popular Teen Patti and Ludo apps, but lighter and less busy so it never distracts from the cards. A relaxed tabla and soft madal groove over light modern drums and warm bass, a gentle flute and sitar motif that comes and goes, soft synth pads and plucks. Positive, bouncy and laid-back, around 95 BPM, major key. Loopable, even energy from start to end: no long intro, no breakdown, no ending, no vocals. (Create music: Standard, Instrumental, genre Custom; 26 October 2026)
